claims.statement: For every eligible lower-region pair (T,p) with T=K_{1,m}, m>=4, every original leaf is selected and S(T,p)=m*(binom(m-1,p)-binom(m-1,p-1))<0.
claims.scope: The ordinary star family only, under x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1.
claims.reason: The zero-extended independence counts give x=floor((m-1)/2)+1; the selector is all leaves, and the residual marked counts are adjacent binomial coefficients in their decreasing range.

claims.statement: Injectivity of the mark-preserving incidence down map on every selected residual's rank-(p) marked-face space would imply the full primary sum S(T,p)<=0; the general-tree injectivity premise remains open.
claims.scope: For H_v=T-{v,s_v}, W_v=N_T(s_v)\{v}, and k=p-1, with the contract's fixed selector.
claims.reason: The dimensions of the marked-face spaces equal q_v(j), so local injectivity yields the needed rank inequality. A Boolean-lattice dimension obstruction shows that injectivity is not available at arbitrary ranks, but not at an eligible rank for the target.

limitations: No injectivity or alternative aggregate rank inequality is proved for arbitrary eligible tree residuals.
The exact dimension obstruction is outside the selector-eligible ranks and is not a counterexample to the primary aggregate.
The star family is only a proved subcase; no universal lower-region conclusion follows.
